correctness.rationale: Every deleted clique fiber must be completely emptied to alter the base index set; maximal independent sets in the remaining expansion project bijectively in cardinality onto maximal independent sets of the surviving base graph. This gives exact deletion transfer and q-fold minimality. The cycle cuts into paths whose independent domination numbers are ceilings of lengths divided by three; an exhaustive residue case split proves no smaller deletion changes the number and identifies all sign-changing minimum gaps. Stars-and-bars with exact cyclic-rotation multiplicities proves both counts. Boundary cases n=3 and q=1 are included. Standalone exhaustive algorithms agree through n=30 for the gap enumeration, through n=11 for independent-set checking, and on direct small clique expansions. Finiteness of tests is not used as a proof.

value.rationale: The existing numerical 1/2/3 stability result leaves its minimum witnesses completely uncounted. The cubic number k^3 and its unequal increasing/decreasing split quantify how often the smallest vertex disruptions change independent domination in opposite directions, while the full-fiber transfer identifies the exact impact of blow-up size on robustness. These counts are natural sensitivity data for graph parameters and distinguish the claim from a routine invariant substitution.
